items: Calculate Your Financial Exposure, Item 1: Determine your exact liability by adding your roommate's portion plus accumulated late fees as specified in your lease to get your real exposure number.

Calculate Your Financial Exposure, Item 2: Create a liability worksheet listing your monthly rent, your roommate's share, your state's maximum late fee, how many days past due the payment is, and your lease's grace period terms.

Calculate Your Financial Exposure, Item 3: Review your lease to identify grace period terms, state-mandated late fee caps, and your joint and several liability clause that makes you responsible for the full amount owed.

Calculate Your Financial Exposure, Item 4: Know your state's landlord mitigation requirement so you understand that your landlord cannot let the debt accumulate indefinitely without attempting to re-rent the unit.

Document Your Responsible Behavior, Item 1: Keep screenshots of every payment you made with timestamps showing you paid your portion on time throughout your tenancy to demonstrate your reliability as the responsible tenant.

Document Your Responsible Behavior, Item 2: Save all text messages and emails where you requested payment from your roommate, including dates and specific amounts requested, to prove you tried to resolve the shortfall directly.

Document Your Responsible Behavior, Item 3: Keep copies of every landlord notice you receive, your written responses to them, and any written commitments your landlord makes regarding your separate liability from your roommate.

Document Your Responsible Behavior, Item 4: Create a detailed timeline documenting every rent payment date, when you first noticed the shortfall, every attempt to contact your roommate, and all landlord communications about the situation.

Execute Your Exit Strategy, Item 1: Send your landlord a formal written letter stating you are the responsible tenant who paid your share on time, and request separation from your roommate's lease obligation before eviction proceedings begin.

Execute Your Exit Strategy, Item 2: Ask your landlord whether you can sign a new individual lease or be released from the current joint lease so your rental history remains intact for future applications.

Execute Your Exit Strategy, Item 3: Document the condition of your unit with photos and videos before you leave, and request a formal walkthrough inspection with your landlord to protect your security deposit.

Execute Your Exit Strategy, Item 4: Prepare a professional explanation for your next rental application that frames this situation as handling a difficult circumstance responsibly through documentation and prompt landlord notification.
